table.name: dpm: slip target straight line offset
table.description: A fixed extra slip allowance, in 1/8 % steps (u8_slip_1/8pct), added to the pedal-derived target dpm_slip_target_from_pedal to give the final dpm_slip_target. It's only applied while flag bit 2 is clear. dpm_system_state_manager_200hz sets that bit when the left/right wheel-speed difference exceeds CAL_dpm_lr_diff_cornerning_threshold, which means the car is cornering. So the car gets more wheelspin before TC cuts torque when driving straight, and when cornering the offset drops out, the target falls back to the pedal value, and TC steps in earlier to protect lateral grip. The on/off delays (CAL_dpm_direct_mode_on_delay / _off_delay) stop it from flickering on and off at corner entry and exit.

table.name: dpm: torque cut i gain
table.description: Calibration: driver performance mode integral gain.

table.name: dpm: torque cut i limit
table.description: Calibration: driver performance mode integral limit.

table.name: dpm: torque cut p term
table.description: dpm_torque_cut_factor is the proportional part of the GT430's ECU traction control. Once the filtered slip error (how far wheel slip is above the target) passes CAL_dpm_intervention_threshold, the ECU looks it up in the 6×10 table CAL_dpm_torque_cut_factor. That table is indexed by front-axle speed, which is effectively vehicle speed since the fronts aren't driven, and by slip error in 1/8 % steps. The ECU adds it to the integral term dpm_torque_cut_accumulated, capping the sum to form dpm_torque_cut_total. That total sets how much of dpm_torque_when_tc_activated (the combustion torque captured when TC first stepped in) is removed. The result is torque_limit_dpm_spark, floored at CAL_dpm_torque_min_allowed, and the throttle limit is set a margin above it.

table.name: ign: target step advance accel pedal ips
table.description: ign_target_step_advance — how fast timing comes back. This table sets the rate limit on ignition timing moving in the advance direction: when the ECU's timing target rises above what's currently being run, this is the biggest bite it's allowed to take, and it takes one bite every 50 ms. Values are quarter-degrees, so degrees per second = value × 5 — a stock value of 8 means the ECU will only feed timing back in at 40 °/s. It's looked up on RPM × accelerator pedal, and stock is a flat 8 (40 °/s) across most of the map, rising to 12–40 (60–200 °/s) only at high RPM with the pedal down. Raise it and timing is restored faster, giving a sharper reconnect out of a cut, but push it too far and the torque returns as a bump instead of a build. Lower it and recovery is smoother, but the engine sits retarded longer than it needs to and feels soft and lazy after shifts or interventions. The high-RPM, high-pedal cells are the ones worth raising for a crisper reconnect; leave the light-pedal cells slow.

table.name: ign: target step advance accel pedal manual
table.description: ign_target_step_advance — how fast timing comes back. This table sets the rate limit on ignition timing moving in the advance direction: when the ECU's timing target rises above what's currently being run, this is the biggest bite it's allowed to take, and it takes one bite every 50 ms. Values are quarter-degrees, so degrees per second = value × 5 — a stock value of 8 means the ECU will only feed timing back in at 40 °/s. It's looked up on RPM × accelerator pedal, and stock is a flat 8 (40 °/s) across most of the map, rising to 12–40 (60–200 °/s) only at high RPM with the pedal down. Raise it and timing is restored faster, giving a sharper reconnect out of a cut, but push it too far and the torque returns as a bump instead of a build. Lower it and recovery is smoother, but the engine sits retarded longer than it needs to and feels soft and lazy after shifts or interventions. The high-RPM, high-pedal cells are the ones worth raising for a crisper reconnect; leave the light-pedal cells slow.

table.name: ign: target step retard accel pedal
table.description: ign_target_step_retard — how fast timing gets pulled. Same rate limit in the opposite direction: when the timing target drops, this is the largest amount of timing the ECU may remove per step, again one step every 50 ms, again in quarter-degrees, so degrees per second = value × 5. It's on the same RPM × pedal axes and it's by far the more pedal-sensitive of the two. Stock is just 2–4 (10–20 °/s) at light pedal, climbing through 8, 16 and 32 to 40 (200 °/s) as the pedal opens, and the whole 4000 RPM column is set to 255 — a step large enough that the rate limit is effectively switched off above that speed. The slow light-pedal numbers are deliberate: pulling timing quickly at cruise makes a hole you can feel for no benefit. The fast high-pedal numbers exist because a target drop under load usually means something that needs to act immediately. Raising the light-pedal cells buys quicker response at the cost of drivability; lowering the high-pedal cells slows down the very interventions you want fast, so be conservative there.

table.name: misfire: baseline default select
table.description: When it acts: EEPROM_load (line 16749) checks it at every start-up. If the learned data is valid and the coding hasn't changed, but the stored LEA_misfire_baseline_set differs from this CAL, it calls init_lea_misfire_baselines(). So flipping this calibration wipes the learned misfire baselines on the next key-on and reseeds them from the other factory set. Leaving it alone keeps whatever the car has learned.

table.name: torque: limit base factor
table.description:
// Used in cylinder cut calculation // "42/255 is the amount of torque reduction per cylinder from a hard cut" (0xff - torque_limit_base_factor) * (6 - torque_cut_level_as_cyl_count)
What It Represents
This is the base torque capacity/efficiency factor at each RPM×load operating point. It's used to:
1. Compare against external torque requests - torque_limit_external_factor (from TC, ABS, stability control) 2. Calculate cylinder cuts needed - when external request is below base factor, determines how many cylinders to cut 3. Define engine torque envelope - maps where the engine can produce full torque vs. derated
